clue.text: Middle-earth character's last but one to leave old kingdom

indicators.note: something that leaves goes away, so the named letter drops out of the name

parts.note: the ranger who becomes king in Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings
the penultimate letter of the character's name

explanation.surface: A Tolkien hero is leaving an ancient realm.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the penultimate R from ARAGORN leaves ARAGON.
explanation.definitionFit: Aragon was a medieval kingdom in north-east Spain, later united with Castile.

clue.text: Bearing lance very clumsily

indicators.note: something done clumsily is fumbled, so the letters fall into a different order

parts.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A knight carries his lance very awkwardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearing' looks like carrying the lance, but it is the definition in its sense of relation or connection.
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing in the sense of 'has a bearing on' means pertinence or connection, which is relevancy.

clue.text: He's an annoying fellow, and damn smart

parts.note: gad is a mild old oath, as in 'by gad'
fly is informal for sharp or knowing

explanation.surface: An irritating man who is also fiendishly clever.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadfly is a persistent irritant or provocative critic, named after the biting fly.

clue.text: Dark part of moon revealing something dreadful

parts.note: darkness, the time after sunset
a mare is one of the dark plains on the moon's surface, Latin for sea

explanation.surface: The shadowed side of the moon shows something terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a frightening dream, and by extension any horrifying experience.

clue.text: One's being pursued by an extremely irascible skinflint

parts.note: one as the speaker, oneself
taken as written

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of irascible

explanation.surface: Someone is being chased by a very bad-tempered miser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's being pursued by' means ME comes first, followed by the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A meanie is an informal word for a stingy, ungenerous person, just like a skinflint.

clue.text: Saying Bottoms up! and losing inhibitions

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top
inhibitions are restraints on the outside, so the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drinker toasts 'Bottoms up!' and gets uninhibited.
explanation.walkthrough: BOTTOMS without its edge letters is OTTOM, which reversed in this down light gives MOTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto is a short phrase expressing a principle, a saying.

clue.text: A soldier perhaps beset by insects in hot city

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something beset is surrounded on all sides, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: lice are small parasitic insects
a soldier ant is one caste of ant

explanation.surface: A soldier is plagued by bugs in a sweltering town.
explanation.definitionFit: Alicante is a sunny port city on Spain's Costa Blanca.

clue.text: Idi Amin heartlessly mistreated us

indicators.note: mistreated means handled badly, so the letters are jumbled
without a heart means the middle letters of the word are removed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; its two middle letters are removed

explanation.surface: The Ugandan dictator Idi Amin cruelly abused us.
explanation.walkthrough: AMIN loses its heart MI to leave AN; IDI plus AN rearranged gives I AND I.
explanation.definitionFit: In Rastafarian speech, I-and-I is used for we or us, stressing unity of people with God.

clue.text: Male setter could be a person of obstinate courage!

parts.note: a bull is a male animal, e.g. of cattle or elephants
a setter is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A man who sets crosswords might be a tenacious, brave sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' tempts you to think of the crossword compiler; here it is the gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Bulldog is used of a tenacious person who refuses to give up, as in 'bulldog spirit'.

clue.text: Mass support for Labour's early childhood assessment

indicators.note: in a down clue, a support goes underneath, so this piece is placed below

parts.note: labour is the process of giving birth
mass and weight are used loosely as synonyms

explanation.surface: Bulk backing for the Labour Party is an early test of its prospects.
explanation.definitionFit: A newborn's weight is one of the first measurements taken of a baby.

clue.text: Carried out cull and conserved a quarter of herd in captivity

indicators.note: something held in captivity is shut inside, so one piece is enclosed by another

parts.note: food conserved in cans is tinned

indicators.note: a four-letter word's quarter is a single letter, here the opening one

parts.note: one of the four letters of herd, the first

explanation.surface: A farmer culled animals but kept a quarter of the herd penned up.
explanation.definitionFit: To thin a population of animals is to reduce its numbers by culling.

clue.text: Software add-ons containing new and ultimately important instructions

parts.note: DOS is the disk operating system, early PC software

indicators.note: containing means holding within, so further letters are taken inside

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of important

explanation.surface: Computer extras arrive with fresh and essential guidance.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking N and T into ADD-ONS gives the right letters but not in order; they need rearranging, which the clue does not signal clearly.
explanation.definitionFit: Dos and don'ts are rules of conduct, a set of guidelines on what should and should not be done.

clue.text: Our Valerie is not disposed to read Marx and Engels, for example

indicators.note: disposed means arranged or set out, so these letters are set out afresh

parts.note: fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A woman called Valerie has no inclination to read communist theory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is not disposed' reads as an unwilling Valerie, but 'disposed' alone is the signal and 'is not' is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Marx and Engels, authors of The Communist Manifesto, are examples of revolutionary thinkers.

clue.text: Suspend half those quoted in share index

indicators.note: half means only one of two equal parts is kept and the other discarded

parts.note: the Hang Seng index lists the shares quoted on the Hong Kong stock exchange

explanation.surface: A trader suspends half of the shares listed on an index.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hang Seng is Hong Kong's main stock market index; its first half is HANG.
explanation.definitionFit: To hang something is to suspend it from above.

clue.text: Beast's exotic ivory made into a musical instrument

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so the letters come out in an unfamiliar form

parts.note: six letters to rearrange
ivory is tusk material, loosely horn

explanation.surface: An animal's foreign tusk has been carved into an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The basset horn is a tenor member of the clarinet family, used by Mozart.

clue.text: Tiny group's resistance is not of great importance

parts.note: a direct synonym
a bee is a social gathering, as in a sewing bee
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A small band's opposition counts for little.
explanation.walkthrough: Small beer is a British idiom for something trivial, originally weak beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Small beer describes anything trivial or unimportant, from the old name for weak ale.

clue.text: Best boy getting beaten

parts.note: to best someone is to outwit them
Ted, a common boy's name

explanation.surface: The finest lad is being thrashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Best boy' looks like a film-crew title or a superlative; 'Best' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To be outwitted is to be beaten by someone cleverer.

clue.text: Chief priest greeting monarch with a bow

parts.note: an informal hello
Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
an arch is a bow-shaped curve

explanation.surface: A senior cleric greets the sovereign and bows.
explanation.definitionFit: A hierarch is a high priest or senior church ruler, as in hierarchy.

clue.text: Disease inflaming eyes, lips and ears, essentially

indicators.note: inflaming suggests heating and agitating, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core of the word, its middle letters

parts.note: the two central letters of ears

explanation.surface: A disease that inflames the eyes, lips and ears.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is also a fair description of the illness, which causes red swelling of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Erysipelas is a bacterial skin infection causing red inflamed patches, often on the face.

clue.text: Farm in deepest Udaipur

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word and the start of the next

explanation.surface: A farm somewhere in the heart of the Indian city of Udaipur.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is a farm where horses are kept for breeding.

clue.text: Climbs ranges

definitions.meaning: first meaning: goes up a wall or mountain
second meaning: graded series, as of notes in music

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read like a mountaineer's day, but 'ranges' is a noun meaning graduated series.
explanation.definitionFit: The word works as a verb for ascending and as a plural noun for graded series of notes or values.

clue.text: Its date could be Gordon's choice

definitions.text: Its date could be Gordon's choice

parts.words: Its date could be Gordon's choice
parts.note: surface reading: an event someone named Gordon gets to schedule
setter's reading: Gordon Brown, UK Prime Minister in 2007, who could pick when the country went to the polls

explanation.walkthrough: In 2007 there was much speculation over whether Prime Minister Gordon Brown would call an early national vote; a UK prime minister could then choose its timing.
explanation.definitionFit: The national poll that chooses a new parliament had its date set by the sitting prime minister.

clue.text: Indian regularly coming to Japan to meet a martial arts expert

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of Indian
J is the international vehicle code for Japan
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Indian travels often to Japan to see a karate master.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a Japanese warrior trained in stealth and the martial art ninjutsu.

clue.text: Frenchman turned up with unknown Brit

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Émile, simplified here, is a typical French man's name
y is a standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A Frenchman shows up with a mystery Briton.
explanation.definitionFit: Limey is American and Australian slang for a British person, from the limes sailors ate against scurvy.

clue.text: Puzzle requiring sharpness and a certain kind of memory

parts.note: a sharp flavour or smell
random-access memory in a computer

explanation.surface: A brain-teaser that needs a sharp mind and good recall.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangram is a Chinese dissection puzzle of seven flat shapes rearranged into figures.

clue.text: The soil could produce old stones

indicators.note: could produce suggests the letters might be turned into something new

parts.note: seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Digging the earth may turn up ancient stones.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true, which makes it a neat fit.
explanation.definitionFit: Eoliths are crudely chipped flints once thought to be the earliest human tools.

clue.text: 60% of Thais invested in bank in China

indicators.note: money invested in a bank is put inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a cay is a low bank or reef of sand

indicators.note: sixty per cent of a five-letter word is three letters, so the last two go

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some Thai people have put money in a bank in China.
explanation.definitionFit: Cathay is an old, poetic name for China, from medieval European travellers.

clue.text: Vigorous desire to live

indicators.note: vigorous suggests energetic stirring, so the letters are shaken up

parts.note: six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A strong will to stay alive.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to have one's home there, to dwell.
